summary: Phase 4 re-audit passes at c1e84b19: the orchestrator disposition resolves blocking finding F1. Provenance: git rev-parse HEAD gives c1e84b19dd1b6a73b9b5ac3c1f5dbe394f88c9be, equal to the audited head, with phase_base_sha 024cfdf9250384667142481856d17eebca91cb15 and role_base_sha a49058531ed2224c55210c90aca45b81d823d44e (test-strategy.md line 5), so the audited HEAD is current. The two commits since be89dc91 touch only plan.md (6 insertions) and green-p4.log (1 line): 43c44210 adds a Phase 4 evidence paragraph and a second unchecked closeout task 'Regenerate measure/generated/ with ./measure/generate.sh and commit it (deferred to the closeout role; blocked while measure/generated/ and measure/tracks.md hold foreign uncommitted edits; Review C F1 at be89dc91)', and c1e84b19 adds the generated_facts_deferral line to green-p4.log. The disposition facts hold: git status shows measure/generated/architecture.json, measure/generated/asset-inventory.json, measure/generated/status.md, and measure/tracks.md modified with foreign uncommitted edits, and git diff --stat counts 1,114 changed lines in the working-tree asset-inventory.json from other sessions; node measure/tools/generate.mjs --check (read-only) still exits 1 with the three stale-fact lines; the committed asset-inventory.json still holds 6 accepted against 36 in the TSV. Judgment on the disposition: acceptable. A write-mode regenerate now would rewrite measure/generated/ files that hold other sessions' uncommitted work, and any commit of them would carry foreign edits, which breaks the standing rule 'Commit only assigned paths during concurrent work' (AGENTS.md). Green could not fix F1 without breaking a stronger rule, so deferral is the correct disposition, and it is recorded in both places the framework reads: the plan closeout task citing Review C F1, and the green log. The stale file is a derived artifact; the source record (the TSV) is correct and complete at HEAD. check-records.sh still exits 0 with 44 PASS at c1e84b19. Judgment on the gate: the catch is partial and human, not mechanical. plan_closeout_feedback in the orchestrator interphase checker exempts any task line whose text contains 'deferred' (it gives no feedback and counts as covered), and closeout_feedback runs neither ./measure/doctor.sh nor generate.mjs --check, so the mechanical closeout gate passes even if the regenerate is skipped. The only lines that name the stale fact are the doctor freshness error and generate.mjs --check, and the doctor line names measure/generated/asset-inventory.json, not the track — the same scoped-grep blind spot as the earlier F2. The stale line can never clear without the regenerate, so a closeout steward who requires the doctor green, or every error line owned, will catch it; nothing mechanical fails on it. Verdict: pass, with the gate blindness carried as a nonblocking item for the orchestrator and closeout steward.
